commits.message:
fix(color): a blend is a colour ColorSpec.parse reads back, named by what its ends draw (rich-strip-hxet)

Review of #263: ColorBlend's name was not parseable, so Style.toString no
longer round-tripped, and it spelled ends as written, so vanishes told
blue- and color(4)-mixes apart. blend(a,b,t) is now a colour form, its name
canonical (slot or hex per end). Ends are opaque and never default:
GradientJoiner ramps between drawn grounds and treats default as nothing to
paint, as PowerlineJoiner does, which drops the flattenAlpha override and
the fg/bg role.

fix(strip): a gradient between named colours ramps between the theme's shades (rich-strip-hxet)

GradientJoiner resolved its two neighbours' backgrounds to RGB at render
time, where the only table is VGA's, so under ATOM_ONE_DARK `on blue` |
`on red` exported as #61afef and #e06c75 with a #000080→#800000 ramp
between them.

Each sample is now `ColorSpec.blend(left, right, t, false)`: a colour that
stays a mix of its two ends until it is drawn. An export resolves both ends
against its theme; a terminal is told the standard-table mix, as before.
The ends are read as backgrounds whoever draws the mix, so an `on default`
neighbour is the theme's background even in a sample used as a foreground.

The powerline seam test compared two theme-drawn colours by palette slot
number, which a mix and the default both lack; they now compare by name
when neither has a slot.

fix(padding): a string handed to a padding draws its markup (rich-padding-wv28) (#262)

* fix(padding): a string handed to a padding draws its markup (rich-padding-wv28)

new Padding("[bold]Hello[/]", 1) threw: Padding took only a renderable, so
docs/padding.md wrapped every string in renderMarkup(). Its body now crosses
embed(), the one crossing a panel, tree, column and layout already use, and
takes string | RichText | Renderable as Rich's takes any RenderableType.
Padding joins the site table in embed.test.ts.
